quests.question: ___ platform the company selects, migrating existing data will take several months.
quests.hint: This word means 'no matter which', introducing a choice among specific options.
quests.explanation: 'Whichever' means 'no matter which' — regardless of the specific platform chosen, migration will take months.

quests.question: The upgrade improves performance ___ it removes the most common bottlenecks in the system.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the improvement extends.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' means 'to the extent that' — the improvement is limited to removing these specific bottlenecks.

quests.question: The rollout succeeded ___ engineers had already resolved every issue found in testing.
quests.hint: Thorough preparation explains the smooth rollout.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a result — resolved issues caused the successful rollout.

quests.question: ___ takes over the department will inherit a talented but overworked team.
quests.hint: This word doubles as the subject of the verb right after it, and means 'no matter who'.
quests.explanation: 'Whoever' means 'no matter who' and also functions as the subject of 'takes over' — the other options cannot serve as a subject this way.

quests.question: The old system rewarded individual output, ___ the new one measures team collaboration instead.
quests.hint: Two systems are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two systems measuring two different things.

quests.question: Team leads now hold shorter daily check-ins ___ issues surface before they escalate.
quests.hint: Holding shorter check-ins has one clear, intended purpose.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces a purpose — the shorter check-ins are meant to catch issues early.

quests.question: Painful ___ the treatment was, most patients said it was worth the long-term relief.
quests.hint: This word can directly follow a fronted adjective — its closest relative usually cannot fit this exact pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Though' can follow a fronted adjective in this inverted pattern — 'although' does not fit this specific structure as naturally.

quests.question: The two treatments produce similar results, ___ one requires a much shorter recovery time.
quests.hint: Meaning 'except that', this phrase isolates the one detail that differs.
quests.explanation: 'Save that' means 'except that' — it introduces the single specific difference between two similar treatments.

quests.question: ___ early detection improves outcomes significantly, screening is now recommended annually.
quests.hint: An accepted fact is the basis for a health recommendation.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an accepted fact as the basis for a decision — better outcomes from early detection justify the recommendation.

quests.question: ___ has the new drug reduced symptoms, but it has also lowered the relapse rate significantly.
quests.hint: Placed first in the sentence, this phrase forces the subject and helper verb to swap places.
quests.explanation: 'Not only' at the front of a sentence triggers inversion — here matched with 'has' for the present perfect tense.

quests.question: The pilot clinic served a small population, ___ the full program will reach the entire region.
quests.hint: Two phases of the same program are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two phases with two different scales.

quests.question: The side effects were mild, ___ the doctor still monitored him closely for a week.
quests.hint: A minor detail didn't remove the need for caution.
quests.explanation: 'But' introduces a contrast — mild side effects didn't stop careful monitoring.

quests.question: ___ the announcement finally comes, markets are expected to react sharply.
quests.hint: This word means 'no matter when', introducing a time that isn't yet known.
quests.explanation: 'Whenever' means 'no matter when' — regardless of the exact timing, the reaction is expected to be strong.

quests.question: The policy will succeed ___ neighboring countries also commit to similar targets.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the policy's success extends.
quests.explanation: 'To the extent that' means the same as 'insofar as' — success is tied specifically to shared commitment from neighbors.

quests.question: Talks stalled ___ neither delegation was willing to compromise on the key demand.
quests.hint: A refusal to compromise explains the stalled talks.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a result — the lack of compromise caused the stall.

quests.question: ___ unlikely the scenario, emergency planners still prepare a detailed response for it.
quests.hint: This word means 'no matter how' when placed directly before an adjective.
quests.explanation: 'However' can mean 'no matter how' before an adjective — different from the linking-adverb 'however' used with a semicolon.

quests.question: ___ that the technology was unproven, several cities agreed to pilot the new transit system.
quests.hint: This legal-sounding phrase works like 'although', but fits formal or official writing best.
quests.explanation: 'Notwithstanding that' introduces a formal concession — despite being unproven, several cities still agreed to the pilot.

quests.question: ___ longer the delegates negotiated, ___ less likely a compromise seemed.
quests.hint: This structure pairs one rising degree with a matching rising degree.
quests.explanation: 'The...the' shows that one change causes a matching change — more time led to less optimism.

quests.question: ___ the inquiry ultimately concludes, public trust in the institution has already suffered.
quests.hint: This word doubles as part of the clause right after it, and means 'no matter what'.
quests.explanation: 'Whatever' means 'no matter what' — regardless of the inquiry's conclusion, the damage to trust has already happened.

quests.question: Local newspapers once covered council meetings in detail, ___ most now barely mention them.
quests.hint: Two eras of local journalism are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two very different levels of local coverage.

quests.question: The correction ran on the front page ___ the original error had been so widely shared.
quests.hint: The scale of the mistake explains the prominent correction.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason for a decision — the widely shared error caused the front-page correction.

quests.question: Reluctant ___ they were, most residents eventually accepted the new parking rules.
quests.hint: This word can directly follow a fronted adjective — its closest relative usually cannot fit this exact pattern.
quests.explanation: Only 'though' fits directly after a fronted adjective like this; 'although' needs a different word order.

quests.question: The two neighborhoods face similar challenges, ___ one has far less access to public transport.
quests.hint: This formal phrase means 'except', introducing the one point of difference.
quests.explanation: 'Save that' means 'except that' — it introduces the single specific difference between two similar neighborhoods.

quests.question: Parking complaints kept rising, ___ the council finally reviewed the entire permit system.
quests.hint: Ongoing complaints directly led to an official review.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces a result — persistent complaints caused the council to act.

quests.question: ___ did the new policy reduce complaints, but it also freed up spaces for residents.
quests.hint: This opening phrase is the only one of the four that flips the normal subject-verb order.
quests.explanation: Fronting 'not only' forces the subject and helper verb to swap places — none of the other options behave this way.

quests.question: ___ most complaints came from a single street, officials focused their response there first.
quests.hint: An accepted fact is the basis for where officials focused first.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces an accepted fact as the basis for a decision — the concentration of complaints justified the focus.

quests.question: The new rules help ___ they free up spaces near the school during drop-off times.
quests.hint: This formal phrase sets a specific limit on how far the new rules help.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' means 'to the extent that' — the benefit is limited to this specific time and location.

quests.question: ___ drafts the final report will need to reconcile several conflicting sets of data.
quests.hint: This word doubles as the subject of the verb right after it, and means 'no matter who'.
quests.explanation: 'Whoever' means 'no matter who' and also functions as the subject of 'drafts' — the other options cannot serve as a subject this way.

quests.question: ___ that early estimates were overly optimistic, the final results still exceeded the revised targets.
quests.hint: In formal writing, this phrase concedes a fact while the main outcome still stands.
quests.explanation: 'Notwithstanding that' introduces a formal concession — despite overly optimistic early estimates, the final results still exceeded expectations.

quests.question: The initial estimate assumed steady conditions, ___ the final figures reflect several unexpected disruptions.
quests.hint: Two sets of figures are being formally contrasted.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally contrasts two related facts — two estimates shaped by two different circumstances.
